cells.date: Śaka 1353 (current), Viśvākṣit, Mārgaśira śu. 5, Sunday= 1431 A.D., November 10 (The week-day was Saturday).
cells.remarks: States that while Aṇṇappa, son of Devarāja Maṅgalurārāya on the orders of Pradhāna Hariyappa-daṇṇāyaka-uḍeya, his subordinate Kriyāratidēva who was administering Tiḷuṇādi during his visit to Puttūr made grant of a brahmadāya land to Pāda-mūlika-naffōjī Subhaṁṇa who was one of the brothers hailing from the bank of river Puḷinā. The donee is stated to be worshipping god Mahādēva installed by himself. The grant was made to the request of Senameya when the image was buried in the earth probably owing to a disaster. The brahmadāya land which was purchased from Padyapa-arasa of the Baṅga for 223 niṣāha at a place called Kambala-timāru is stated to have been given in perpetuity with the condition that the taxes are to be paid in the prescribed time.

cells.remarks: Indifferently engraved. States that it is the grant made by Nirvāṇa-svāmi of Subrahmanya to Nīlakaṇṭha Kallūrāya Sitārāma-bhaṭṭa of Nīlāvara. The purport of the record seems to register the permission to construct a dam near the Kolavaliki village situated in Kodumbala over the river Komarādhāra for the purpose of providing water thorough a canal for growing gardens of cocoanuts, mangoes, plantains etc. It also states that leaving the 2,000 trees which were given freely to him he has to pay for the rest at the rate of 5 honnu for each thousand trees. The donee is also stated to have received the office of Hebbārka along with the above grants.

cells.dynasty: Copper-plates now preserved in the Department of Ancient History, Culture and Archaeology, Nagpur University. Set No. 1. Findspot : Maṇḍal, Nagpur District, through Dr. S. Subramonia Iyer.
cells.remarks: The western road from Padmapura at the request of Āryya Mahādēvi to Mahā[pu*]rusha (probably a deity) to the place for whom two shares have been allotted and the rest to brāhmaṇas viz. Boppāryya who belonged to Kauṇḍinyasagōtra, Viṣṇuvāryya and Ratyāryya of Bhāradvāja-gōtra, Bhavāryya and Bhavaputrāryya of Parāśara-gōtra, Gōlāryya and Śrīyāryya of Bhāradvāja-gōtra, Boppāryya of Kāśyapa-gōtra, Nārāyaṇayya and Suvalāryya of Kauśika-gōtra, Dēvāryya and Dāmāryya of Kauṇḍinya-gōtra, Kēśīvāryya and Vatsakumāryya of Kauśika-gōtra, Dāmāryya of Kāśyapa-gōtra, Gōlāryya of Kauṇḍinya-gōtra, Gōlāryya of Kāśyapa-gōtra, Kōṭṭiryya and Rudrāryya of Gautama-gōtra. Records also another grant of twenty-five measures of land situated on the western side of the village probably Mattakadraha to god and brāhmaṇas by the king. The sēnāpati at that time was Kātyāyana and the ājñapti was Dēvasakha.

cells.place: No. 3.
cells.remarks: Issued from his camp at Beṇṇātaja. Records the royal grant of the village Gōvasāhikā in the uttara-pajja (northern bank probably of Beṇṇa) and bounded on the east by Śulkavaṭa, on the south by Kurubhēṇijaka, on the west, by Beṇṇā-nadi and on the north by Pidērikā to four brāhmaṇas Mahēśvarasvāmin, Brahmasvāmin and Harasvāmin of the Kautsa-gōtra and to Varāhasvāmin all belonging to Beṇṇātaja. The grant was made at the dharmasthānā for obtaining merit evidently of the king here as well as in the other world. The sēnāpati at that time was Vishṇudatta. The charter was written by Śarvvadatta.

cells.remarks: Gives the genealogy of the Yādava kings of Dēvagiri up to Rāmachandra. Also mentions the genealogy of his minister Sthānu-chāmū-pati and the titles assumed by him. Records the renewal of the grant of the village Bobbēnakapalli in Magatala-vishaya after the renovation of the same by Sthānu for worship and offerings to the deity Svayambhū Mallinātha of Magatala. The record was composed by Vishṇusūri, a disciple of Advayānanda-Kṛishṇa and written by Viṭhhaya-mantri. Published in Hyd. Arch. Series, No. 19, Mn 25.

CHÁPAPALALLE-Contd.
cells.remarks: of the brāhmaṇa donees, one share as vēda-vṛitti and lands endowed as dēvadāna for the deity Tirunāgīsvaram-uḍaiyār and as tiruvi-daiyātam for the deity Yādavanārāyanap-perumāl, set up by the chief. It is stated that the agaram originally created by the chief in the 39 th regnal year of Kulōttunga III was expanded by adding lands nearby in lieu of lands elsewhere belonging to the lady and donated for the purpose in the next year i.e. the 2nd year of Rājarāja (III). The foundation of the agaram is stated to have been made through the good offices of Madhurāntakap-pottappichōlan Era-Siddharasar whose niece the lady is stated to be. It is further stated that the inscription was caused to be engraved by the lady on the maṇḍapa built by herself. Ibid., Part III, Venkatagiri Nos. 1 and 10.

cells.place: Broken pillar standing in front of the Māruti temple outside the fort, first face.
cells.date: Chāḷukya Vikrama year 50, Viśvāvasu, Phālguṇa śu.... Thursday
cells.remarks: Mentions at the top the names of Mallisetti, Sireya Kāḷišeṭṭi and Guṇavīra-siddhāntadēva. Records the construction of a basadi and the installation of the deity Pārśvādēva at Āḍaki by Daṇḍāyaka Kopparasa along with a number of seṭis and the ascetic Guṇavīra-siddhānta-dēva. Also records the grant of garden and land for the worship and offerings, aṣhavidhārcchana, and for the occasions of Jīvadayāshṭami, Nandīśvaradāshṭami, Samikramaṇa and Grahaṇa for this and the Teṅkaṇa Koppa-Jinālaya at Āḍaki by Kopparasa Daṇḍāyaka and gift of oil for maintaining perpetual lamps in both the basadis by the samasta-nakara.

cells.location: PACHARAL
cells.place: A slab built into the wall inside the Sāntinātha shrine.
cells.remarks: Begins with a verse in praise of Sāntinātha. Refers to Bālachandra, the disciple of Subhanandi belonging to Kuṁda-kuridasaṁtāna and Dēśika-gaṇa. Mentions the ruler and his forbears Harirāja and Bhīma. Gives the genealogy of a person named Mahēśvara belonging to Parapāt-ānvaya. His son was [Dē]vi and his son was Rājana, who is stated to have made the kirti (for the image). Mentions at the end two gōṣhṭhikas of which one is named Jasahada. Noticed in Gwalior Rājya ke Abhilekh, No. 45.

cells.place: West wall in the same place.
cells.remarks: Begins with the prasasti Tirumagal-mīvalara etc. States that the assembly (Perunguri) of Vāhūr alias Alagiyasōlach-chaturvēdimangalam met at the Alagiyasōlan-ambalam of the same village on the night of Friday, the first day of the bright fortnight of the month Dhanus combined with the Pūrattādi-nakshatra in the 16th regnal year (1027 A. D. December 1) with Kappūrur Udayār Nilap Veńgadgan of Tiruvaļudūr-nādu in Uyyakkon-darvaļanādu and decided that the tank commitee (Eri-vāriyam) may collect the tax called ēri-āyam in the form of paddy every year and in every season from the cultivating tenants belonging to the villages outside. Also states that the tenants of this village and those settled in this village aged between ten and eighty excluding the untouchable shall each desit from the tank from a pit measuring 2X2X1 kōl of four spans. It was attested by Uttamappiriyan.

PONDICHERRY—Concld.
TRIBHUVANI—Concld.
Tōtādri nātha temple, ruined maṇḍapa, south base, tiers.
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Records an arrangement (vyavasthai) made by the sabhai of Tribhuvanamādēvichaturvēdi-maṅgalam a brahmadēya in Vilupparaiya-nāḍu in Rājēndra-śōla-vaḷanāḍu, according to which the sabhai undertook to collect the taxes on the lands at Pūmbāḍi alias Ālappiranda-śōlanallūr alias Rājādhhirājānallūr, the kāṇi villages of Sēnāpatigal Rājēndraśōla-Māvali-Vāṇadhirāyar at a reduced rate on the basis of the reclassification under the twelfth class. Further states that the lands were lying fallow for the past fifteen years and that under the earlier classification and assessment made 30 years ago not much was left for paying taxes.

cells.remarks: Damaged and incomplete. Contains the carvings of Śūla with a parasol above and auspicious objects like Moon, flywhisk, lamps etc. and weapons and implements of artisans. In characters of the 11th century.

cells.date: Vikrama 1592, Śaka 1457, Māgha śu. 8, Friday, Rêvatî. Irregular.
cells.remarks: Begins with an invocation to Îśāna. Extols Pāśupatāchārya Naraharayati. He is described as having constructed tanks (jalaṁdhārī) temples (suragāṛha) and sculptures(mūrtayah). Records that a magnificent monastery (mathikā) consisting of a secret path (gūdha-mārga), an underground chamber (bhūmi-grihā) and a musical hall (vādya-grihākṛitiḥ) was caused to be constructed by Narahari. Mentions ākāśavāsī Pāśupatāchārya Viśvanātha pañjadhīśvara. The praśasti was composed by paṇḍita Purushôttama of the Daśapurajñāti. The monastery was constructed under the supervision of sūtrādhāra Bhīmasiṁha who was also the engraver of the inscription.

text.remarks: Begins with an invocation to Îśāna. Extols Pāśupatāchārya Naraharayati. He is described as having constructed tanks (jalaṁdhārī) temples (suragāṛha) and sculptures(mūrtayah). Records that a magnificent monastery (mathikā) consisting of a secret path (gūdha-mārga), an underground chamber (bhūmi-grihā) and a musical hall (vādya-grihākṛitiḥ) was caused to be constructed by Narahari. Mentions ākāśavāsī Pāśupatāchārya Viśvanātha pañjadhīśvara. The praśasti was composed by paṇḍita Purushôttama of the Daśapurajñāti. The monastery was constructed under the supervision of sūtrādhāra Bhīmasiṁha who was also the engraver of the inscription.Read more (1 KB)

cells.date: Vikrama 1404 (vēda-Viyat-payōdhi-vidhu) Kārthika śu. 14 Thursday= 1347 A.D., October 18.
cells.remarks: Records the construction of the Dakshiņi Abaya (Dakshiņa Abhaya) and other vihāras by the king who is described as the son of Mahārāja Tissa. In characters of about the 2nd century A.D. Noticed in Ancient Inscriptions in Ceylon, p. 73, No. 5; p. 109, No. 5.

cells.place: No. 2.
cells.remarks: States that this the grave of Maulavī Shāh Muḥammad Isḥāq, Deputy Collector and Magistrate, (eldest) son of late Shāh Ḥusain ‘Alī (see No. 94 above), a descendant of Shāh Muṣṭafā Ṣūfī (see No. 86) and a grandson, on mother’s side, of Maulavī Ṣujā‘u’d-Dīn son of late Maulānā Qiyāmu’llāh. Further states that after completing studies he entered service in his youth, and having progressed day by day, rose to post of Magistrate which he held for fourteen years. Also states that he suffered a heart stroke in the night of the given date, at his headquarters Bānkā, District Bhāgalpūr and expired on the morning of Friday at the age of 35; his body was brought from there, on palanquin and by train, to be interred at his ancestral and sepulchre.

cells.remarks: States that Nawwāb Diler Khān Bahādur son of ‘Abdu’l-Karīm Buhlūl Khān Miyāna granted four Chāwars of land in the town (qaṣba) Bilgi in pargaṇa Bākarkoṭa (Bāgalkoṭ ?) to his servant B(v)isājī Paṇḍit son of Mahdājī and grandson of Bābājī, a Pātālshāhī Rug(v)edī Brahmin (zummārdār), and the latter out of his personal earned income, excavated a step-well and laid out a garden for his merit in the next world, under the supervision of his nephew Kiṣṇājī son of Raghunāth.
